principals.name: Marta Vale
principals.opening: Bram has my shipment tied up at the docks. Help me before evening, and I won't forget it.

principals.name: Elias Ward
principals.opening: Greyhaven keeps its own order. See that you don't disturb it.

principals.name: Father Orin
principals.opening: Words have a longer life than their speakers.

principals.name: Nessa Reed
principals.opening: The tide answers to nobody, least of all merchants.

principals.name: Bram Coyle
principals.opening: Triple is simply what urgency costs.

principals.name: Talia Fen
principals.opening: Most troubles improve when someone arrives before being asked.

principals.name: Pip Marr
principals.opening: You're the newcomer with the royal purse, aren't you? Or was it a royal warrant?

principals.name: Rhea Kest
principals.opening: Elections in three days. The town could use a fresh name—or a useful fool.

ambients.name: Jonas Pike
ambients.opening: Cargo tells you who owes whom, if you know how to count.

ambients.name: Mae Dorr
ambients.opening: A hand that helps before the rain is a hand I remember.

ambients.name: Oswin Bell
ambients.opening: Everyone wants tomorrow's bread on yesterday's credit.

ambients.name: Del Sayer
ambients.opening: The tide brings truth in eventually. Usually smelling worse.

ambients.name: Hettie Voss
ambients.opening: Rhea knows how to keep the market predictable.

ambients.name: Cal Moss
ambients.opening: I vote for whoever keeps customers walking this row.

ambients.name: Edda Grey
ambients.opening: New names make old promises very easily.

ambients.name: Will Harker
ambients.opening: Rhea has faults. At least we already know their price.

ambients.name: Fen Lark
ambients.opening: A mayor ought to know which end of a crate is heavy.

ambients.name: Lina Thread
ambients.opening: Reputation is only a seam. Pull it and see what holds.

ambients.name: Tob Rill
ambients.opening: Buy no speeches before you've heard the second telling.

ambients.name: Kit Wren
ambients.opening: I know who answers a knock and who lets a message freeze.

endings.title: The Town Turns
endings.summary: Greyhaven chooses the newcomer by a margin even Rhea cannot explain away.

endings.title: By One Voice
endings.summary: The final name is yours, carried over the line by the memories you changed.

endings.title: The Tied Bell
endings.summary: Rhea keeps the guildhouse. One changed mind would have changed the town.

endings.title: No Seconding Voice
endings.summary: Your candidacy ends as a story the tavern tells more loudly than your speech.

endings.title: The Story Unravels
endings.summary: The town compares your word with its memory and finds the seam.

endings.title: The Road Remembers
endings.summary: Greyhaven sends you back down the road under a chorus of every threat it kept.

bram_approaches.label: Threaten him quietly
bram_approaches.dialogue: Careful. A threat is a debt Greyhaven collects with witnesses.
bram_approaches.event_text: You threaten Bram over the shipment. The market goes still enough to hear it.
bram_approaches.original_claim: The newcomer threatened Bram over Marta's held shipment.

bram_approaches.label: Flatter his business sense
bram_approaches.dialogue: At last, someone understands that profit and civic virtue can share a ledger.
bram_approaches.event_text: You praise Bram's business sense until his price begins to sound negotiable.
bram_approaches.original_claim: The newcomer publicly praised Bram's business sense to soften his price.

bram_approaches.label: Negotiate a deal
bram_approaches.dialogue: You bargain like someone who thinks witnesses are friends.
bram_approaches.event_text: Your argument with Bram carries farther than either of you intended.
bram_approaches.original_claim: The newcomer confronted Bram about tripling the shipment price.

bram_approaches.label: Lie about a constable's order
bram_approaches.dialogue: Elias never signed such an order. I wonder how long it takes that fact to cross the square.
bram_approaches.event_text: You invent a constable's order. Bram recognizes the lie and lets the market hear it.
bram_approaches.original_claim: The newcomer lied that Constable Elias had ordered Marta's shipment released.

town_events.title: Storm over Greyhaven
town_events.start_text: A harbor storm breaks over Greyhaven. The docks empty and the town crowds into the inn.
town_events.end_text: The storm spends itself before dawn. Greyhaven steps back into its ordinary routes.

active_awareness.nessa: My boats stayed in because I value living crews over drowned cargo. Let the merchants complain.
active_awareness.marta: Every wet soul in Greyhaven is under my roof. Mind whose story you repeat tonight.
active_awareness.pip: Nessa's boats stayed in. Bram says that makes every late crate her fault.

resolved_awareness.nessa: The harbor is open again. The sea took no crew from me, and that is enough.
resolved_awareness.marta: The rain cleared. The stories it drove indoors did not.
resolved_awareness.pip: The storm passed, but Bram's version of it is still making the rounds.

town_events.title: Bram and Nessa in the square
town_events.start_text: Bram and Nessa erupt over storm losses. Greyhaven forms a ring around them in the square.
town_events.end_text: The square breaks into factions as Bram and Nessa carry their grievance away.

active_awareness.bram: Her boats stayed tied while honest cargo spoiled. Sentiment does not balance a ledger.
active_awareness.nessa: Bram would spend a crew to save a crate, then invoice the widows for rope.
active_awareness.pip: Bram blames Nessa for the storm. Nessa says Bram counts drowned sailors as breakage.

resolved_awareness.bram: The square heard enough to know which side understands consequence.
resolved_awareness.nessa: A crowd can leave. A merchant's price still finds you tomorrow.
resolved_awareness.pip: The shouting stopped. The choosing sides did not.

argument_choices.label: Back Bram's claim
argument_choices.dialogue: At least one person in this square understands that choices have a cost.
argument_choices.event_text: You back Bram. The merchants applaud while the harbor folk turn away.
argument_choices.memory_text: The newcomer publicly blamed Nessa for keeping the fleet in during the storm.

argument_choices.label: Defend Nessa's crews
argument_choices.dialogue: Good. A living crew can sail tomorrow. Bram's spoiled numbers cannot.
argument_choices.event_text: You defend Nessa. The dock workers answer while Bram closes his ledger.
argument_choices.memory_text: The newcomer publicly defended Nessa for keeping her crews alive in the storm.

argument_choices.label: Calm the crowd
argument_choices.dialogue: You made peace sound almost interesting. That takes talent.
argument_choices.event_text: You separate blame from loss. The square quiets long enough to listen.
argument_choices.memory_text: The newcomer calmed Bram and Nessa's public argument without choosing a faction.

favors.content: Carry Nessa's storm log to Elias, then correct Bram's story with Pip.
favors.accept_dialogue: The harbor log shows every boat tied before the worst wind. Put it in Elias's hands before Bram makes caution sound like guilt.
favors.complete_dialogue: That log has dates, crew marks, and weather. Bram's version will not survive reading.
favors.correction_text: The harbor log proves Nessa kept the fleet in before the storm and protected every crew.

favors.content: Decide whether to reveal or conceal a dying guild clerk's confession about Rhea's last election.
favors.accept_dialogue: A dying guild clerk named Rhea and swore she changed two marks in the last tally. He gave me leave to act, but not the courage. Carry the truth carefully.
favors.complete_dialogue: What you do with a confidence becomes part of the truth people tell about you.
favors.correction_text: A dying guild clerk confessed that Rhea changed two marks in Greyhaven's previous election tally.

confession_choices.label: Reveal the confession
confession_choices.dialogue: Then let truth have witnesses. Elias will take the statement, but do not mistake a necessary wound for a clean one.
confession_choices.event_text: You reveal the clerk's account before Orin, Elias, Edda, and Will: Rhea changed two marks in the last tally.
confession_choices.memory_text: The player revealed Orin's account that a dying guild clerk saw Rhea alter two marks in the previous election tally.
confession_choices.pip_speech: A dead clerk named Rhea, and the newcomer made Orin say it where Greyhaven could hear.

confession_choices.label: Keep the confession sealed
confession_choices.dialogue: You kept a burden from becoming a weapon. I will tell Greyhaven's elders that your judgment deserves their trust.
confession_choices.event_text: You keep the clerk's confession sealed. Orin publicly blesses your judgment before Edda and Will.
confession_choices.memory_text: The player kept a dying clerk's confession sealed, and Orin publicly blessed that restraint before Greyhaven's elders.
